items.title: Turning Database Grading into RL Rewards: Post-Training Agents with ThinkingBox
items.excerpt:
This is the follow up to our first blog post, The Agent Said It Was Done. The Database Disagreed. ThinkingBox-Training is now available on GitHub .
We built ThinkingBox to evaluate an agent's work by comparing the final database state with the expected outcome. We then used the same kind of executable signal as a reward on training tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench. For Qwen3.8-27B, average success rose from 51.70% to 60.78%, while tasks completed correctly on all twenty attempts rose from 38 to 107 with 50 GRPO steps.
Figure 1. ThinkingBox turns executable checks of terminal database state into rewards for post-training agents on tasks outside ThinkingBox-Bench.
We built ThinkingBox to catch agents that say they are done when they are not.
Each of its 507 tasks in ThinkingBox-Bench (our benchmark dataset) hands an agent a real backend and a set of tools, lets it work, then checks what really changed in the database. In the first post , we caught a model closing a customer's ticket as resolved while the carrier exception behind it was still open. Nine competent-looking tool calls, one wrong database row.
Then we noticed what we had built. For most tasks, an executable check can return 1 or 0 directly from the final database state. That is not just a grader. This can be a reward function. +
So we constructed a training pool from ThinkingBox-format tasks outside the benchmark and used their executable outcomes as rewards. The catch was choosing which tasks are suitable for agent training: most tasks are either already solved or hopeless for the model in front of you, and both teach it nothing.
Difficulty is policy-relative: a task is hard for the current model only until that model learns it.
We call this offline policy-relative difficulty . We estimated each task's success probability once using the base policy before training and kept the selected training pool fixed throughout the run.
We used offline policy-relative difficulty to build the training pool, then fine-tuned Qwen3.8-27B with GRPO for 50 steps. To recap, we evaluate each of the 507 benchmark tasks 20 times. pass@1 measures average success across all 10,140 attempts. pass@20 measures the share of tasks solved at least once. Observed 20/20 measures the share of tasks that pass every recorded attempt.
Table 1. Qwen3.8-27B results before and after 50 steps of GRPO on the offline-selected training pool.

items.excerpt:
Warehousing third party logistics provider says it is building speed and reliability comparable to Amazon Prime.
The warehousing third party logistics provider (3PL) Stord is continuing its acquisition streak just two weeks after taking on $400 million in financial backing, buying the 3PL AMS Fulfillment for an undisclosed amount to mark its 12th takeover.
Valencia, California-based AMS Fulfillment says it processes more than 10 million orders per year for beauty, wellness, and high-velocity direct-to-consumer brands.
Atlanta-based Stord says the deal is its largest acquisition to date, adding over 1 million square feet across key East and West Coast hubs, including the Los Angeles, Salt Lake City, and Philadelphia metro areas, and bringing millions of annual orders onto Stord's platform. Stord's global network now spans more than 100 locations.
Stord had plenty of leverage to make the purchase, following the news that it had secured a $400 million credit facility led by Citi in October , closely after a $250 million Series F venture capital round in May. Supported by the Series F, Stord launched Stord Labs, its dedicated robotics deployment arm and data foundry. Stord is using the capital to expand its fulfillment network across the U.S. and internationally, and to accelerate its investment in robotics and AI at Stord Labs.
Previous acquisitions made by the company include buying Shipwire from CEVA Logistics in January , and in recent years snapping up Fulfillment Works, ProPack, Pitney Bowes E-Commerce Fulfillment, and UPS’ Ware2Go.
"In modern commerce, what happens after checkout has become as important to consumer trust as the product itself," said Sean Henry, CEO and Co-Founder of Stord. "We have spent a decade building the leading fulfillment network and end-to-end commerce platform, leveling the playing field for brands with Prime-like speed and reliability. This year, Stord has added the scale, leadership, network infrastructure, capital, and technology to extend that experience. AMS further accelerates our scale, while bringing some of the most discerning brands in the industry onto our platform. In commerce, scale drives lower costs, faster speeds, and more trust with consumers—powering Stord's flywheel. This deal spins our flywheel even faster, and we are entering peak shipping season with more capabilities, intelligence, and momentum than at any point in our history."

items.excerpt:
Small modular reactors (SMRs) could provide a source of power for cranes through the night, maritime group says.
The American Association of Port Authorities (AAPA) is throwing its weight behind White House efforts to build nuclear reactors at maritime ports, saying the small modular reactors (SMRs) could provide a source of power for cranes through the night.
"We are witnessing an undeniable momentum for nuclear energy at ports across the maritime industry,” Sang Yi, AAPA’s president and CEO, said in a release.
“Key partnerships have emerged across the country to examine port microgrids, shoreside power, and emerging vessel propulsion technology applications. These partnerships envision broader potential for SMRs beyond propelling cargo ships across oceans to include a source of job creation for American workers and a source of power for cranes through the night. A diverse energy portfolio, including expanded grid connections, energy storage, microgrids, and other emerging technologies like SMRs, will be the answer. Undoubtedly, nuclear technology must meet rigorous safety, security, environmental, and regulatory standards. AAPA is working across industries for clear federal permitting responsibilities and strong emergency-response protocols developed with the U.S. Coast Guard through meaningful public and stakeholder engagement. America's ports are gateways to the global economy and require reliable, resilient, and sufficient power to keep American commerce moving," Yi said.
Additional support for the concept came from the ports of Long Beach and Corpus Christi.
"When you look at the different options that are on the table, small modular reactor has already been used by the US Navy for seventy years, it’s been adopted in different sectors and industries across the globe. items.description: Replit 发布 Monitoring Agent，为应用提供相当于自主值班工程师的监控智能体。它可以读取生产日志和指标调查错误、变慢和部署失败，在启用 autofix 后验证修复并邮件汇报，启用 auto-publish 后可自动部署修复。该能力建立在早前上线的 App Monitoring 之上，用户可在应用的 Publishing 设置中开启。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/h1d0qu9nsy86fmfqns5f3pkjb
items.excerpt:
Replit Monitoring Agent: Your very own software engineering team
Replit 发布 Monitoring Agent，为应用提供相当于自主值班工程师的监控智能体。它可以读取生产日志和指标调查错误、变慢和部署失败，在启用 autofix 后验证修复并邮件汇报，启用 auto-publish 后可自动部署修复。该能力建立在早前上线的 App Monitoring 之上，用户可在应用的 Publishing 设置中开启。
原文说明了该智能体如何调查告警、验证修复并部署，可帮助读者判断它能否替代个人开发者深夜值班。
在大公司里，值班工程师会收到寻呼，调查问题，并努力让应用重新运行起来。而对大多数创作者和小团队来说，这份责任落在了同一个人身上——他既要构建产品，又要支持客户，还要努力发展业务。
Replit Monitoring Agent 为每一位内部应用构建者和创业者提供了一个自主的应用值班工程师。
当生产环境出现问题时，Monitoring Agent 可以调查告警、定位原因、制定并验证修复方案，然后将该修复部署到生产环境。之后它会汇报发生了什么以及改动了什么。
今年早些时候，我们推出了 App Monitoring ，在已发布的应用宕机时为你提供生产健康检查和告警。现在，我们要闭合这个循环。当你在 Replit 上运行应用时，你的 agent 不仅会告诉你哪里坏了，还会把问题修好。
现在，你不必再从沮丧的用户那里得知服务中断，而是可以一觉醒来，专注于对你重要的事情，安心于应用的正常运行时间已有人处理。
一旦你的应用进入生产环境，保持其运行就意味着要了解正在发生什么、在出问题时做出响应，并安全地发布修复。
Replit Monitoring Agent 是首个能够为 AI 应用创作者自主查看、修复并部署变更的此类 agent。
Agent 可以访问你的生产日志和指标，从而获得调查错误、变慢和部署失败的上下文，无需你亲自翻查日志。
启用告警和自动修复后，问题发生时 Monitoring Agent 会收到通知。它会调查原因、验证修复，并通过电子邮件向你发送事件摘要。
启用自动发布后， Monitoring Agent 可以部署经过验证的修复，并汇报改动了什么。修复是否自动发布由你决定。
Replit 是首个在云端实现 agentic 编程的平台。随着 agent 能力不断增强，我们的重心正从单一的编程 agent 扩展到 能够完成现代软件工程团队所能做的一切、甚至更多的自主软件团队。
我们相信，软件的未来是由多个 agent 组成的团队协同工作，来构建、维护、保护和优化软件，而创作者设定方向并保持掌控。
在过去六个月里，我们推出了业界领先的系统，用于 黑盒安全扫描 、 增长 ，以及现在的生产监控。这些是迈向自主 agent 团队的重要步骤，这些团队能够管理任何在 Replit 上构建的应用、工具或业务。
所有这些都服务于一个简单的理念：更多人应该能够将自己的想法变成现实。 构建应用只是这段旅程的一部分。保持其可靠、安全、可被发现并持续改进，历来需要一整个团队。通过让每位创作者都能使用能够完成这些工作的 agent，更多人无需成为各个领域的专家，就能创建、发布并发展软件。
你还可以开启自动发布，让 Monitoring Agent 自动部署已验证的修复。

items.title: UK operators search 6.7 times more for CRM and ERP than for cash-cycle tools as factory robots pass five million
items.description: UK operators are searching about 6.7 times more for CRM and ERP software than for the tools that turn completed work into cash, according to a Klipboard analysis of UK search data, at a time when the number of industrial robots working in factories worldwide has reached around five million. The gap matters because every […]
items.excerpt:
UK operators are searching about 6.7 times more for CRM and ERP software than for the tools that turn completed work into cash, according to a Klipboard analysis of UK search data, at a time when the number of industrial robots working in factories worldwide has reached around five million.
The gap matters because every installed robot and production cell eventually depends on field service work: an engineer booked, a fault fixed, a visit signed off and an invoice raised.
The analysis covers UK monthly search volume through August 2026. CRM software draws about 8,900 UK searches a month and ERP software about 5,400, a combined 14,300.
Six cash-cycle terms (invoice software, quoting software, quote software, digital invoicing, invoice chasing and job invoicing) add up to about 2,140. That is the 6.7 times gap.
Gabriel Cohen, VP of Go-To-Market at Klipboard , a field service management platform, said the finding points to a commercial habit rather than a shortage of technology.
“The search bar is still voting for planning suites,” Cohen said. “CRM and ERP draw about 6.7 times the demand of cash-cycle tools, and field service sits near a thousand monthly searches. That is how field work stays busy and finance stays late. The job gets done, the record stays fragmented, and the invoice waits.”
Field service management software, the scheduling and dispatch layer used by engineers who maintain automated plant, sits at about 1,000 UK monthly searches. It is used in the analysis as a labelled baseline and is not part of the 6.7 times ratio.
The physical side of industry has travelled a long way. The International Federation of Robotics reported in September 2026 that around five million industrial robots now operate in factories globally. AI is following the same path.
Figures published by Cisco in April 2026 show 61% of enterprises already using AI in live industrial operations, 20% with deployments scaled to a mature level and 83% planning to increase AI spend. The survey covers firms with more than $100m in revenue.
The weak point is the join between information technology and operational technology. In the same dataset, 57% of organisations report some IT/OT collaboration, while 43% report limited or none.
Among those with limited collaboration, 47% cite network instability as the top challenge to scaling AI, and 40% of respondents name cybersecurity as the biggest obstacle.

Claude 官方宣布，下周起 Pro、Max 和 Team 套餐在 Claude 网页、桌面和移动端应用中的会话将默认以 auto mode 运行。auto mode 不再逐步请求用户批准，而是由自动检查拦截高风险操作，用户可随时切回手动模式。其引用的 Claude Code 更新提到 auto mode 用独立分类器审查 shell 命令，测试中拦截了 89% 的危险命令，手动批准为 14%。
官方说明 Claude 各端默认开启 auto mode 的变化与手动切换入口，读者可据此评估权限模式对日常使用流程的影响。
从下周开始，在 Pro、Max 和 Team 套餐中，Claude 网页版、桌面端和移动应用上的会话将默认以自动模式运行。
系统不再要求你逐步批准，而是通过自动检查来阻止高风险操作。你可以随时切换回手动模式。
Starting August 14, auto mode will be the default permission mode in Claude Code for Pro, Max, and Team users. Auto mode reviews shell commands and actions with a separate classifier. In testing, it caught 89% of dangerous commands. Manual approval caught 14%.

items.title: Warehouse PPE and Hi Vis in the Age of Automation: Keeping People Safe Around the Machines
items.description: Warehouses have changed faster in the past decade than in the previous fifty years. Automated vehicles, robotic pickers and conveyors now share the floor with people. Those people still need protecting, and the right high-visibility workwear is central to that. This guide covers the warehouse PPE the job demands. It also shows why automation raises […]
items.excerpt:
Warehouses have changed faster in the past decade than in the previous fifty years. Automated vehicles, robotic pickers and conveyors now share the floor with people.
Those people still need protecting, and the right high-visibility workwear is central to that. This guide covers the warehouse PPE the job demands. It also shows why automation raises the stakes, not lowers them.
There is no single legal checklist of warehouse PPE in the UK. The right kit comes from a risk assessment of the real tasks and hazards. In practice, most sites need high-visibility clothing, safety footwear and suitable gloves as a baseline.
The law behind this is the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations . Employers must assess the risks and provide suitable PPE free of charge.
Since 6 April 2022, those duties also cover limb (b) workers, meaning casual and agency staff. That matters in warehousing, where agency labour spikes at peak.
It is tempting to assume automation makes a warehouse safer by removing people. On the floor itself, the opposite is often true. Humans and machines now share the same aisles, and that mix creates fresh risk. A human driver makes eye contact; an automated vehicle only follows its sensors and route.
The national picture is sobering. In 2025/26, HSE provisional figures recorded 24 workers killed after being struck by a moving vehicle. That was the second most common cause of workplace death. Transport and storage alone accounted for 15 worker deaths.
Modern sites run a mix of manual and automated transport. Forklifts still move constantly, often under time pressure. Alongside them run automated guided vehicles (AGVs) on fixed routes, and autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) that navigate their own path.
These driverless trucks have their own safety standard, BS EN ISO 3691-4. But a standard cannot see a worker who blends into the background.
Keeping people and vehicles apart through layout is the strongest control, as HSE workplace transport guidance makes clear. Marked walkways, barriers and separate doors all reduce contact. Where paths must cross, visibility does the rest. Blind corners and tall racking hide people. Bright clothing helps a driver or sensor register them sooner.
Warehouses rarely enjoy bright, even daylight. Many run through dark winter mornings, late evenings, or around the clock under artificial light. Visibility clothing earns its place most in exactly these conditions.

items.title: The Verge 分析 SpaceX 与特斯拉成立特别委员会讨论合并背后的财务逻辑
items.description: The Verge 作者 Elizabeth Lopatto 分析 SpaceX 和 Tesla 各自成立特别委员会讨论合并一事。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/w7axcg0e1y7uoyro92cmanong
items.excerpt:
Sure, let’s smoosh SpaceX and Tesla together, who cares
The Verge 作者 Elizabeth Lopatto 分析 SpaceX 和 Tesla 各自成立特别委员会讨论合并一事。
原文梳理了 SpaceX 与特斯拉合并讨论背后的财务动机、Musk 投票权变化和薪酬条款，读者可以借此区分叙事与利益。
哦当然，SpaceX 的 信用风险相当高 ，因为它即将 再借 400 亿美元用于购买 Nvidia 芯片 ，但谁在乎呢？SpaceX 和 Tesla 已成立特别委员会讨论合并事宜！
你觉得这桩合并有多大说服力，大概取决于你在多大程度上相信埃隆·马斯克关于想去火星、或者说“传播意识之光”的说法——他在本周的 SpaceX 财报电话会（以及更早的 S-1）上就是这么说的。如今，一个有一定常识的人都知道，我们并没有技术支持人类在太空生存——坦白说，甚至连构建这项技术的原始信息都没有。所以这意味着要靠机器人。但地球与月球或火星之间的延迟导致控制机器人很困难。因此，拥有能够在极少地球监督下自主决策的人工智能机器人，就是科幻逻辑的下一步。
如果你相信马斯克的故事，我们谈论的技术正通过自动驾驶汽车（Tesla）、LLM（SpaceX）和人形机器人（Tesla）来开发，而所有这些都需要数据中心（SpaceX）。方便的是，我们刚好看过这两家公司的财报。另一方面，如果你把火星视为马斯克用来解释其公开行为的有用虚构，那么，马斯克从这桩合并中能获得大量金钱和大量控制权。
马斯克在最近的 SpaceX 财报电话会上表示，SpaceX 与 Tesla“合并有很多好处”。为什么？“在开发超级智能软件方面合作，能收获很多。”但人工智能——啊，抱歉，是 超级 智能软件 并不是 SpaceX 目前真正从事的业务。 在周二的第三季度财报中，SpaceX 报告称人工智能——抱歉抱歉，是 超级 智能部门实现 75.6 亿美元营收。子类别“SI 解决方案与基础设施营收”——我认为这是把 Grok、Cursor 和新云业务打包在一起——跃升至 70 亿美元，是上一季度的三倍多。其中一部分来自 并入 Cursor ，后者贡献了 6.08 亿美元营收。DA Davidson 分析师 Gil Luria 表示，这 70 亿美元中的其余大部分很可能是向 Anthropic 和 Google 出租算力；Grok 的贡献可能较小。
乍看之下，这似乎与 Anthropic 这类公司的营收相当，后者 泄露的 S-1 显示，该公司今年上半年从前沿模型获得了 163 亿美元营收。但 SpaceX 的 AI 业务看起来更像 CoreWeave ，而不是 Anthropic。虽然新闻稿中告诉我们“Grok 在企业客户和消费者中的采用率有所提高”，但这一数字并未从裸金属营收中单独列出。而如果马斯克想炫耀这一点，他早就这么做了。
至于周三发布第三季度财报的特斯拉，其盈利表现糟糕——连续第二个季度利润下滑。这是因为马斯克显然对普通汽车不再特别感兴趣了。相反，特斯拉正专注于机器人，以及，我猜，自动驾驶出租车。（最近还有一场 Roadster 蹦跳汽车演示 ，但那款车几年内都不会投产，价格非常昂贵，而且 特斯拉无法保证它能交付 。）马斯克在特斯拉电话会上没有详细阐述他关于合并的言论。
SpaceX 和特斯拉之间已有一些合作；例如，SpaceX 购买了价值 1.31 亿美元 的滞销 Cybertruck。它过去还持有过特斯拉债券。更关键的是，两家公司还共同宣布了两个 AI——算了，我们就沿用 AI 这个说法——项目：Terafab 和 Macrohard。
Terafab 是马斯克 打算在得克萨斯州建造 并运营、为自己供应芯片的芯片制造项目；英特尔与马斯克算是合作伙伴，共同开发这项技术。Macrohard 则是一个 AI 项目，让人们 模拟微软已经做出来的软件 。至少我认为它应该是这个意思。打出后一个名字让我祈祷小行星现在就撞上我们所有人，所以也许幸运的是，自 3 月宣布以来我们没怎么听到它的消息。
“马斯克有设定时间表而旗下公司未能兑现的历史，” 路透社 指出，带着一种我只能形容为挖苦式轻描淡写的语气
5 月的 SpaceX S-1 文件 称，Terafab 和 Microhard“处于非常早期的阶段，因此我们和特斯拉尚未敲定与我们的合作相关的各种细节，包括但不限于财务条款、知识产权以及我们合作的最终期限。”截至本月早些时候，英特尔 CEO 表示公司 仍致力于这一合作 ，但英特尔没有义务继续留在 Terafab 中，而 S-1 文件称可能永远不会有最终协议。英特尔发言人 Thomas Hannaford 没有立即回复我询问在此期间是否签署了任何协议的邮件。
在本周与 SpaceX 投资者的电话会上，马斯克声称 Terafab 将在 2028 年下半年 实现量产。他还表示，公司将在 2027 年 5 月或 6 月从该工厂获得首颗测试芯片。“马斯克有设定时间表而旗下公司未能兑现的历史，” 路透社 指出，带着一种我只能形容为挖苦式轻描淡写的语气。当电话会上一位分析师询问马斯克是否已订购制造尖端设备所需的机器时，马斯克没有回答。
公司私下做的事情往往比公开宣布的更多，所以我不认为 S-1 文件完全具有决定性。但最近一份 10Q 中没有提到 Macrohard。也没有提到 Terafab。
马斯克会拍着桌子大谈月球、火星、“以及更远的地方”，他的相当一部分粉丝对此非常买账。但股东们可能出于一些无聊的财务原因而对此感兴趣。
假设你在体质上与我截然不同，而且富有得多，因此你持有一些特斯拉的股票。你显然是埃隆·马斯克的忠实信徒——但你也注意到，这个人的注意力持续时间就像一只吸了可卡因的松鼠。他基本上时刻都在X上，而且常常带着种族主义色彩。他不断出现在白宫，做些惹恼潜在特斯拉客户的事情。然后他又公开与总统交恶。有时他对火箭兴致勃勃，有时又对狗狗币

items.title: Google DeepMind uses Gemini 4 Argon to teach Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid new skills from video
items.description: Google DeepMind has demonstrated a new robotics training technique in which its Gemini 4 Argon AI model learns a physical task by watching video and then transfers the resulting behavior to Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid robot. The demonstration forms part of the launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s latest frontier AI model, which the company says […]
items.excerpt:
Google DeepMind has demonstrated a new robotics training technique in which its Gemini 4 Argon AI model learns a physical task by watching video and then transfers the resulting behavior to Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid robot.
The demonstration forms part of the launch of Gemini 4 Argon, Google’s latest frontier AI model, which the company says combines visual-semantic reasoning, physical understanding and autonomous code generation for robotics applications.
In an internal test, Argon was shown raw video of a person playing cornhole. The model analyzed the environment, mapped its spatial coordinates and calculated the whole-body joint movements required to perform the task.
Argon then autonomously generated simulation code before the learned behavior was transferred to Apptronik’s Apollo humanoid.
According to Google DeepMind, Apollo subsequently landed seven consecutive shots during a real-world trial.
The company describes the approach as a “Video-to-Sim-to-Real” pipeline and says it can reduce a robotics simulation process that would normally require weeks of manual work to a few hours.
Google DeepMind says: “This ‘Video-to-Sim-to-Real’ pipeline compresses weeks of manual simulation modeling into a few hours, transforming ordinary videos into a scalable, infinite training ground for robotics.”
The demonstration is intended to show how general-purpose AI models could reduce the amount of manual engineering required to teach robots new physical skills.
Google DeepMind also tested Argon on its Embodied Reasoning benchmark, or ERQA, which measures a model’s ability to reason about physical and spatial problems in 3D environments. The company says Argon achieved a score of 87 percent.
Gemini 4 Argon is being positioned more broadly for complex engineering, scientific, coding and business tasks. Google says it has already used the model for projects ranging from optimizing large software codebases to quantum computing, nuclear fusion and life-sciences research.
The model is now being made available through Google’s AI products and Gemini API, with Google presenting the robotics work as part of a wider effort to apply advanced AI reasoning to physical systems.

items.excerpt:
Swedish robotics startup 120ft has emerged from stealth after raising €576,000 in angel funding to develop autonomous microfactories using humanoid robots for local manufacturing.
The Stockholm-based company is developing modular factories designed to enable consumer brands to assemble products locally in smaller batches rather than relying on large production runs and lengthy international supply chains.
Founded in 2025 by Martin Willers, 120ft plans to operate its factories itself, with customers paying per finished product rather than purchasing robots or establishing their own automated production lines.
The company’s factory design uses three 40-foot containers for component preparation, assembly, inspection and packing – giving 120ft its name.
Its system combines humanoid robots, AI, virtual production-line simulation and proprietary orchestration software. Product designs, parts lists and quality requirements are converted into digital instructions, allowing assembly processes to be tested virtually before production begins.
120ft says it has reduced the time required to teach one end-to-end robot assembly skill from seven weeks in 2025 to seven hours in 2026. Its target is seven minutes in 2027.
The company has demonstrated the system by using robots to assemble a lamp, including installing a cylinder lock, threading the bulb fitting and carrying out a functional test.
Willers, founder and CEO of 120ft, says: “I started 120ft because I had lived this problem myself. At Transparent, we could spend months waiting for thousands of products to arrive before knowing what colour customers actually wanted the most.
“For a smaller brand, that means tying up cash and making decisions about demand far too early. Robotics and physical AI are now reaching the point where we can rethink that model.”
The funding comes from 22 angel investors, including Ted Persson, co-head of EQT’s Scaleup Europe Fund; Sophia Bendz, partner at Cherry Ventures and former global marketing director at Spotify; Fashwell co-founder Matthias Dantone; and Sam Baker of Planet A.
Baker says: “A robot on its own does not solve the manufacturing problem. Brands also need the tooling, software, quality control and operational systems around it.
“120ft is bringing those pieces together into something customers can simply buy as finished production.”

items.title: OpenAI 正式发布 Decisions API，面向低延迟低成本小决策
items.description: OpenAI 宣布基于 GPT-6 Luna 的 Decisions API 正式可用，用于分类、路由、评分等有界答案问题，速度最高比通过 Responses API 使用 GPT-6 Luna 快 10x。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/xffhf8h0e0r145getmi9k1zgs
items.excerpt:
Build more responsive apps with the Decisions API
OpenAI 宣布基于 GPT-6 Luna 的 Decisions API 正式可用，用于分类、路由、评分等有界答案问题，速度最高比通过 Responses API 使用 GPT-6 Luna 快 10x。
官方宣布 Decisions API 正式可用，给出与 GPT-6 Luna 的速度对比、定价和 GPT-Live 集成，便于评估路由分类类场景的收益。
应用和智能体在整个工作流中会做出许多小决策：如何对输入进行分类、将请求路由到哪里，或接下来采取哪个操作。单独来看，它们都很简单。但在规模化场景下，它们的延迟和成本会不断累积。
今天，我们正式全面推出 Decisions API。Decisions API 基于 GPT‑6 Luna 构建，将 Luna 的智能聚焦于答案有界的问题，帮助应用和智能体基于文本、图像和结构化输入做出近乎实时的决策，通过 Responses API 比 GPT‑6 Luna 快最多 10 倍。
自公开测试版以来，我们新增了原生 GPT‑Live 集成、针对重复使用上下文的提示缓存，以及美国和欧盟的推理驻留。开发者还可以传入原生 JSON 输入、在问题指令中包含图像，并且每个请求最多可提出 400 个问题，是此前上限的两倍。我们还持续改进延迟，包括在亚洲多个地区增加容量。
在 OpenAI 内部，各团队正在将 Decisions API 应用于产品和业务工作流。dots 团队用它来缩短响应时间并提升交互性。我们的个人财务团队用它来对交易描述进行分类，而我们的传播团队则用 Decisions 按主题对报道进行分类并评分，判断其是强化还是挑战关键叙事——帮助识别哪些内容值得进一步审查。
这些早期示例表明，快速、结构化的决策如何将传入信息转化为广泛用例中的有用行动。客户对 Decisions API 的应用同样广泛，从准确归因 AI 成本到让语言学习体验更具互动性。
“_借助 Box Extract 和__Decisions API，我们对业务文档进行分类，并将其路由到正确的下一步。在我们的评估中，_ Decisions API 在 30 个保险证书案例上实现了约 5 倍更快的路由选择，准确率与__Responses API 相同——自动化常规工作，并将置信度较低的案例发送给审核人员。 ”
“ Decisions API 帮助我们在执行智能体生成的 [ rshell 命令⁠（在新窗口中打开） ] 之前对其风险进行评分，从而自主修复问题。与可用的前沿模型相比，它以相当的准确率实现了快 40 倍的 p95——使 Decisions 能够置于修复操作的热路径中。 ”
“ 与 GPT‑6 Luna 相比，Decisions API 将我们的 AI 成本归因到实际工作的速度提升了 4 倍，成本降低了 30%，且不牺牲准确率。 ”
“ 在 Sierra，我们在实时客户对话中编排的部分环节使用 Decisions API 来选择正确的下一步操作。它以低于 280 毫秒的 p95 运行，比我们之前的方法快约 3 倍，每次调用成本降低 90%，且客户结果没有下降。 ”
“对于语言学习者来说，时机至关重要。在我们的测试中，GPT‑Live 中的 Decisions API 集成能够将下一步行动的时间缩短 90% 以上，从 1.4 秒降至 0.13 秒，从而创造出更具互动性的学习体验。”
使用 Decisions API 非常简单：开发者定义一个问题和其允许的答案，然后以文本、图像或原生 JSON 形式提供上下文。该 API 会返回三种受支持的答案类型之一——概率、选择或评分——应用可据此决定接下来发生什么。多样的答案类型使 Decisions 能够适用于广泛的使用场景。
借助 GPT‑Live ，你可以为语音应用带来自然、富有表现力的对话，并具备流畅的打断处理能力，让对话保持连贯。Decisions API 现已 与 GPT‑Live 原生集成⁠（在新窗口中打开） ，帮助应用在实时对话中做出快速、聚焦的决策。客服智能体可以决定是否提出澄清问题、转接请求或升级问题。虚拟形象可以在用户对其说话时调整面部表情，并根据用户的话语以眨眼或微笑回应，从而创造更具互动性的体验。
下面的示例使用转录更新来选择虚拟形象的表情。将此配置添加到现有 GPT‑Live 会话中的 session.triggers 。
1{2 "type": "decisions",3 "event_type": "session.input_transcript.delta",4 "decisions": {5 "questions": [{6 "type": "choice",7 "name": "reaction",8 "instructions": "Choose an appropriate reaction for the avatar based on the user's latest message.",9 "choices": [10 { "value": "neutral" },11 { "value": "happy" },12 { "value": "sad" },13 { "value": "concerned" }14 ]15 }]16 }17}
Live 会发出一个 decision.event ；应用读取所选的 reaction 并相应地驱动角色动画。 了解更多关于将语音连接到 Decisions API 的信息。⁠（在新窗口中打开）
此演示有时间限制。使用即表示你同意 OpenAI 的 条款⁠ 并确认我们的 隐私政策⁠ 。
Decisions API 现已通过专用的 Decisions 端点正式提供，并支持 GPT‑6 Luna。当前费率与缓存详情请参阅 定价与可用性指南⁠（在新窗口打开） 。

items.excerpt:
Worldwide investment in dual-fuel ships exceeds $200 billion as containership lines and vehicle carriers move toward low-emission equipment, WSC data show.
More than 500 dual-fuel containerships and vehicle carriers are operating worldwide, with total investment in dual-fuel ships delivered and on order surpassing $200 billion, according to the latest World Shipping Council (WSC) Dual-Fuel Fleet Dashboard , released today.
The report shows 503 dual-fuel ships in use as of September, up more than 40% from 358 at the same time a year ago. Another 849 ships are on order, bringing the total delivered or on order to 1,352 ships, according to WSC.
Dual-fuel ships are designed to operate on either conventional marine fuels or alternative fuel types, including renewable and lower-emission fuels, helping to prepare the fleet for the transition to cleaner shipping.
The latest figures highlight companies’ efforts to make that transition despite a lack of regulatory guidance that industry watchers say would accelerate the move to cleaner fuels.
“The container ship and vehicle carrier industry have committed more than $200 billion to ships that can run on cleaner fuels, with more than 500 already sailing and hundreds more on the way,” Joe Kramek, president and CEO of the World Shipping Council, said in a statement Thursday. “The investment is happening, but these ships need commercially competitive alternative fuels to deliver their full potential to reduce emissions.”
The latest figures show that alternative-fuel-capable ships remain the dominant choice for containership and vehicle carrier orders. They account for 65% of containership orders and 97% of vehicle carrier orders, as measured by deadweight tonnage. That compares with 23% across the rest of the global shipping fleet.
The report also shows that orders for conventional-fueled ships have increased compared with a year ago—a move that comes amid continued uncertainty over global GHG regulation at the International Maritime Organization (IMO). The WSC said it supports a global greenhouse gas measure through the IMO as part of that organization’s 2023 GHG Strategy . Such a measure would help close the cost gap between conventional and alternative fuels and provide clear, consistent rules for international shipping, according to WSC.
Without that framework, the industry risks facing a patchwork of regional emissions regulations that will add cost and complexity to global trade, the group also said.

The finalists pitched at the challenge’s Demo Day during the Electronic […]
items.excerpt:
Infineon has named Italian robotics startup AdapTronics as the winner of its 2026 Startup Challenge, which focused on technologies for humanoid robots and physical AI.
More than 100 startups from 29 countries entered the competition, with 15 selected to develop and present their technologies. The finalists pitched at the challenge’s Demo Day during the Electronic Based Systems Conference (EBSCON) in Graz, Austria.
AdapTronics took first place with a gripping technology designed to enable robots to handle a variety of objects without conventional suction cups or mechanical grippers. Infineon says the technology could have applications in humanoid robotics as well as logistics, packaging and space robotics.
Lorenzo Agostini, founder and CEO of AdapTronics, says: “Winning the Infineon Startup Challenge is a great recognition of our team’s work and vision.
“The challenge gave us valuable access to technology experts, industry insights and a strong innovation network. We look forward to further advancing our solution and exploring new opportunities for collaboration.”
South Korea’s COSMOKE took second place with COSKIN, a flexible magnetic tactile sensing technology designed to give humanoid robots information about touch, pressure and physical interactions. The technology is intended to support dexterous manipulation and safer human-robot interaction.
German startup TECHiFAB placed third with an in-memory computing approach to real-time motor control for robotic actuators. The company says the technology can provide faster and more energy-efficient control within humanoid robot drivetrains.
Infineon provided the participating companies with hardware and software platforms covering environmental sensing, artificial skin, motor control and visual feedback, as well as its in-house AI development software.
Sören Jehmlich, vice president ventures, startups and ecosystems at Infineon, says: “Strategic collaboration with startups creates a win-win situation, combining novel ideas with industrially proven semiconductor technologies and thereby accelerating innovative, market-ready applications.
“The Startup Challenge is a key pillar of our innovation culture, bringing together entrepreneurial courage, technological expertise and rapid implementation.”

items.title: Microsoft AI 发布 SDBench 基准与 MAI-DxO 诊断系统，登 Science
items.description: Microsoft AI 发布 Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark（SDBench）和 AI 诊断系统 MAI-DxO，论文发表于 Science。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/r7uwz6n0sd6jr2r0tb1fu3o0u
items.excerpt:
Microsoft AI 发布 Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark（SDBench）和 AI 诊断系统 MAI-DxO，论文发表于 Science。
原文给出 SDBench 基准与 MAI-DxO 的具体准确率和成本数据，并开放部分评测代码，读者可据此评估其诊断推理方法。
如果 AI 能帮助临床医生逐步完成复杂的医学诊断，并以更低的成本、更少的医学检查实现更高的准确率，会怎样？
这一未来正逐渐成为现实。在美国急诊科的常见就诊病例中，使用 MIMIC-IV-ED 的病例进行评估时，我们的 AI 诊断系统 MAI-DxO 的准确率是医生的 1.7 倍。
而在发表于 The New England Journal of Medicine 的医学最复杂病例中，MAI-DxO 的准确率是使用教科书和互联网的医生的两倍以上——当医生在没有这些资源的情况下进行诊断时，其准确率接近四倍。它还能以一半甚至三分之一的成本做到这一点，用更少的检查和操作得出正确诊断。
本周还发表在 BMJ Digital Health and AI 。 上的文章介绍了我们对医疗超级智能的愿景，可阅读更多内容。
AI 有潜力变革健康与医疗保健，相关进展正在迅速加快。当前的挑战在于构建并严格评估 AI 系统，将其临床推理能力的进步转化为有意义的影响。
今天的论文 建立在早期工作之上 ，i 提出了这一转变的两项基础：顺序诊断基准（SDBench），用于测试逐步诊断推理；以及 Microsoft AI Diagnostic Orchestrator（MAI-DxO），这是我们在该基准上表现领先的 AI 系统。
诸如 美国医师执照考试 （USMLE）等医学执照考试旨在评估医生的知识——而非进行临床诊断的现实情况。在这些考试中，所有信息都会预先给出，并选择一个答案；而在实践中，临床医生必须逐步构建整体情况，决定要询问什么、开具哪些检查，以及每项新发现如何改变可能的诊断。此类考试已成为评估健康 AI 性能的常见基准 。
这就是我们开发 SDBench 的原因，它通过两组互补的病例评估性能：取自 The New England Journal of Medicine （NEJM）病例报告的 304 个复杂病例，以及来自 MIMIC-IV-ED 的一组更典型的急诊科就诊病例。每个病例都会成为一个交互式病例，AI 模型和/或医生从有限信息开始，并选择接下来请求什么。该基准衡量诊断准确率、请求的证据和估计的检查成本——同时评估答案和所采取的路径。
我们构建了 MAI-DxO，并在 SDBench 中对其进行了测试。它并非依赖单一模型立即给出答案，而是像一组虚拟医生那样运作：每位医生提出诊断、选择有用的问题或检查，并对逐渐形成的观点提出质疑。MAI-DxO 在数轮辩论中协调这一交流，随着证据出现更新其评估，并权衡每项检查的可能价值与成本。
我们正在开源 SDBench 用于部分 NEJM 病例——包括基准、Gatekeeper、Judge 和成本估算代码——以便研究人员能够复现评估、测试其他模型，并对这些发现提出挑战或加以扩展。
诊断只是照护旅程的一部分。更好的照护还需要跟上医学知识、选择正确的治疗、理解随时间发生的变化，并支持反映个人价值观和照护可及性的选择。机会在于将这些能力统一为一种当今尚未广泛可用的照护标准。在发表于 BMJ Digital Health and AI 的 The Building Blocks of Medical Superintelligence 一文中，我们探讨了 AI 需要具备什么才能支持这一更宏大的愿景——并最终超越当今最强临床团队和卫生系统的能力。
序贯诊断提供了一个早期示例：AI 医生协作、质疑假设，并随着证据出现完善其临床推理。我们的目标是构建在整个照护旅程中连接知识、情境和决策的 AI——而不仅仅是在某一项临床任务上表现出色。通过与 Mayo Clinic 的合作，我们旨在结合前沿 AI、临床专业知识和纵向多模态数据，构建能够应对真实世界照护复杂性和多样性的系统。
基准测试固然重要，但真正的考验是在真实临床环境中的表现。通过与波士顿的 Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center 建立新的合作关系，我们将在不同医院环境中评估临床推理能力。在一项前瞻性研究中，患者将直接与系统互动，其表现将对照医生的独立评估进行衡量。与临床团队并肩工作将揭示这项技术在哪些方面取得成功、在哪些方面存在不足，以及它如何融入繁忙的工作流程。
医疗 AI 的快速进步正在为患者和临床医生带来新的可能性。为了将这一进展转化为实际影响，我们正汇聚微软各健康团队——包括 Microsoft Research 的科学家以及 Dragon Copilot 和 PowerScribe 等产品背后的团队——在 Microsoft AI 形成一体化协作。通过携手合作，我们将加速交付值得信赖的 AI 系统，推动更好的临床结果和护理体验。
我们是一个精干、行动迅速的实验室，汇聚了世界上一些最有才华的人才。我们在 MAI 拥有一份令人振奋的算力路线图，正在快速且大规模地扩展。我们还有一个我们真正相信的雄心勃勃的使命。我们也很幸运能与出色的产品团队合作，让我们的模型有机会触达数十亿用户并创造巨大的积极影响。如果你是一位才华横溢、雄心勃勃且不摆架子的人，你会非常适合这里——快来加入我们，一起打造我们的下一代模型！
原文给出 SDBench 基准与 MAI-DxO 的具体准确率和成本数据，并开放部分评测代码，读者可据此评估其诊断推理方法。

items.title: Why AI Compute Comes in Rectangles — Erik Bernhardsson, Modal CEO
items.description: Elastic GPUs, sandbox growth, and the economics of the agent cloud
items.excerpt:
Warm welcome to Basil Chatha , our newest cohost from the Forward Deployed side of the AI Engineering world! We’ll be ramping up a new show with him and couldn’t pass up an interview with Modal’s CEO Eric on the occasion of their monster Series D!
Two years ago, we spoke with Erik Bernhardsson about his vision for truly serverless AI infrastructure: developers should be able to run code without provisioning clusters, predicting load, or paying for idle resources. CTO Akshat then joined us to talk about Modal’s infra primitives and stack to offer those primitives and agent experience.
A lot has changed in the past 5 months. Since their $5B series C, Modal now reports it crossed $1 billion in annualized run rate , raised a $750 million Series D at a $16B valuation , and has spun up nearly three billion sandboxes. In this conversation, Erik joins Vibhu to explain the infrastructure and economics behind that growth—and why demand for compute rarely looks like the contracts used to buy it.
A typical capacity contract gives a customer a fixed number of GPUs for a fixed period. Plot capacity against time and you get a rectangle. Real workloads behave differently: they grow, spike, and fall throughout the day. Buy enough for the peak and you pay for idle hardware; buy less and you risk missing demand.
Erik describes Modal’s bet as a kind of duration transformation: pool demand across thousands of customers, secure capacity underneath, and let each customer use what they need when they need it. The smoother the aggregate demand, the more useful that pool can be. It’s a useful companion to our conversation with SF Compute’s Evan Conrad : Evan focuses on making capacity tradeable; Erik focuses on making it usable in smaller, elastic slices.
There is a financial risk on the other side. If a provider locks in capacity at today’s prices and GPU prices later fall, it can be left holding expensive supply. Erik says he doesn’t expect an imminent collapse, but thinks the possibility matters when building the business. Jump to the GPU price discussion →
Modal launched sandboxes after Erik and cofounder Akshat Bubna noticed that language models could generate code—and that someone would need a place to run it. Early adoption was modest enough that the team discussed shutting the product down. Then coding agents, background agents, and reinforcement learning created new demand. items.title: The Autonomous Logistics Network
items.description: The autonomous logistics network will not arrive as a warehouse with no people or a fleet with no drivers. It will not be switched on one morning after a company installs an AI platform. It will emerge incrementally as more routine logistics decisions stop waiting for human coordination. The post The Autonomous Logistics Network appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The autonomous logistics network will not arrive as a warehouse with no people or a fleet with no drivers. It will not be switched on one morning after a company installs an AI platform.
It will emerge incrementally as more routine logistics decisions stop waiting for human coordination. The path toward autonomy therefore depends on the discipline described in Engineer AI Into the Decision : authority, context, optimization, and control have to be designed together.
That is the logical conclusion of the architecture explored throughout this series. Physical assets become more observable. Execution systems become more connected. Visibility moves toward interpretation. Orchestration coordinates decisions across domains. AI handles increasingly complex information. Agents perform bounded work. Automation executes more physical tasks.
Autonomy is not a destination. It is a spectrum of delegated operational authority.
Everything begins with the physical network: trucks, trailers, containers, warehouses, docks, robots, conveyors, roads, ports, and people. These assets create the hard constraints of logistics. Capacity, distance, time, labor, infrastructure, and physics remain real regardless of how sophisticated the software becomes.
The autonomous network therefore does not replace the physical layer. It uses information and decision-making to employ that layer more effectively.
TMS, WMS, YMS, OMS, warehouse execution and control systems, and global trade applications remain the mechanisms through which much of logistics work is planned and executed. The autonomous architecture does not require one system to replace them all.
It requires those systems to expose enough state and enough controlled action for decisions to move across boundaries. A transportation event must be able to influence warehouse execution. A warehouse constraint must be able to influence transportation. A trade event must be able to influence order and inventory decisions.
Connected vehicles, sensors, telematics, RFID, computer vision, equipment data, carrier feeds, and enterprise events create a continuously changing digital picture of the operation.
This layer answers the first question of autonomy: What is happening?
Its weakness is uncertainty. Data can be incomplete, delayed, or wrong. Autonomous systems therefore need not only observations but confidence in those observations.

items.title: Lucas Systems partners with CMU to advance algorithmic logistics planning
items.description: Lucas Systems and CMU are researching new ways to use data to help operators manage distribution centers more efficiently. The post Lucas Systems partners with CMU to advance algorithmic logistics planning appeared first on Automated Warehouse .
items.excerpt:
While warehouse automation is maturing, there is still plenty of opportunity for innovation. Lucas Systems Inc. this week said it has partnered with Carnegie Mellon University, or CMU, on new data analysis research to help warehouse supervisors make accurate and productive workforce decisions.
“Warehouse managers are drowning in data but starving for insight. They’re making million-dollar decisions based on experience and gut feel because the data they have isn’t organized in a way that tells them what to do next,” stated Kent Szalla, vice president of software engineering and customer success at Lucas Systems.
“What excites me about this research is that it points toward a future where the system surfaces the right signal for planning at the right moment,” he added. “Supervisors aren’t guessing; they’re deciding.”
Founded in 1998, Lucas Systems said its warehousing software is designed to advance distribution centers ‘ ability to compete in ever-changing market conditions. The Wexford, Pa.-based company said its customers can harness the power of data with AI , machine learning, and optimization models for operational agility and improved performance.
Despite an overabundance of warehouse data, operators still lack the tools necessary to fully use data insights to manage labor and tasks efficiently, according to Lucas Systems.
“The landscape is so complex and requires such constant observation that it becomes impossible to rely on human decision making,” said the company . “Modern problems require a more sophisticated approach that only smart technologies can provide.”
Lucas Systems said its research with the university could have significant commercial impact for thousands of companies in the logistics industry. As part of the project, master’s level students in the Spring 2026 cohort of CMU’s Master of Science in Applied Data Science provided prediction models after studying hundreds of data attributes related to warehouse users and behaviors.
“They collaborated with us on the very complicated math,” said André Lessa, director of research and development at Lucas Systems. “As a result, we have a strong foundation to realize our vision.”
Lucas Systems data scientists and software engineers said that using these perspectives “could be a game-changing leap forward in an industry still overly reliant on guesswork and tribal knowledge when it comes to planning.”

items.title: Opinion: Send the robot, not the person. What inspection robots are really for
items.description: By Daniela Shchegelskaya, an electronics engineer at Elimpus who has spent the last two years working with Boston Dynamics’ Spot for hazard-zone inspections in live power substations When presenting my robotics work, two questions regularly emerge. Do we really need robots? What will happen to field service engineers? I can understand why people are concerned, […]
items.excerpt:
By Daniela Shchegelskaya , an electronics engineer at Elimpus who has spent the last two years working with Boston Dynamics’ Spot for hazard-zone inspections in live power substations
When presenting my robotics work, two questions regularly emerge. Do we really need robots? What will happen to field service engineers?
I can understand why people are concerned, but rest assured: my robotics work centers on keeping engineers safe and outsourcing hazardous tasks to machines.
I want the knowledge that can only be obtained by a human engineer to remain central to the work, and I also want fewer people to have to enter places where they may be seriously harmed.
I worked as an electronics engineer at Elimpus, where I tested and adapted Boston Dynamics’ Spot (main picture) for power-substation inspection, including carrying partial-discharge monitoring equipment. It is an ongoing proof-of-concept project.
Our goal was to adapt a robot to collect information from hazardous areas, reducing engineers’ exposure to dangerous conditions and having inspections be carried out remotely and more quickly.
At a substation, the engineer’s task is gathering evidence about the condition of equipment and deciding whether something needs attention. In my ideal world, a robot can gather some of that evidence and ensure that a human remains far from hazardous conditions.
It is not necessary or even likely that a robot take over every part of that inspection. It may carry an instrument to a location or provide a more detailed view of equipment. Then, the engineer can review the information and decide what further investigation may be needed.
Some tasks still require an engineer on site. For example, diagnostic equipment may need to be calibrated manually at the inspection location, which the robot in our current setup cannot do. Sending the robot to collect readings therefore does not remove every reason for an engineer to attend.
This is how I think about the division of work. A trained engineer should be able to use their expertise without every observation requiring them to stand beside the equipment. But we need to preserve the information they would normally use to make sense of what they find. Moving the person away from the hazard also moves them away from some of the context.
In one of my projects, vibration prompted engineers to investigate a possible problem on site. When they went to investigate, they found that nearby roadworks were the source.

items.excerpt:
Cerence , a developer of conversational AI-powered user experiences, has announced that its collaboration with Geely is expanding from intelligent cockpits to embodied robotics, with the two companies working together to advance multilingual human-machine interaction for robotics applications.
The collaboration with Geely – one of China’s largest automakers – brings Cerence AI’s production-proven speech and conversational AI technologies into physical AI.
As intelligent machines move from controlled environments into real-world settings, natural interaction becomes critical not only to how people experience these systems, but also to how effectively people and machines work together.
Whether assisting customers, supporting workers, or engaging with the public, intelligent systems must be able to understand, respond, and collaborate naturally with the people around them.
Building on decades of experience delivering voice and AI technologies for the automotive industry, Cerence’s robotics solutions leverage production-grade, multilingual conversational AI to help machines listen, understand, and respond reliably across languages, environments, and use cases.
The collaboration marks the expansion of Cerence AI’s work with Geely from intelligent cockpits to service robotics, and makes its public debut at the Paris Motor Show.
Cerence AI’s multilingual speech recognition supports French, English, and Mandarin simultaneously, enabling users to interact naturally in their preferred language without interrupting the experience.
Christian Mentz, chief revenue officer at Cerence AI, says: “For decades, Cerence AI has helped people communicate naturally with the machines they rely on every day.
“Through our collaboration with Geely, we are bringing proven human-machine interaction technologies into the emerging robotics space and helping shape the future of how people engage with these intelligent systems.”
The collaboration reflects Cerence AI’s continued expansion beyond automotive and underscores the growing importance of natural, multilingual interaction as intelligent systems become more integrated into everyday life.
By combining Geely’s robotics strategy with Cerence AI’s expertise in conversational AI and human-machine interaction, the companies are taking an early step toward enabling more intuitive experiences across the next generation of physical AI systems.

items.title: Managing 3PL Ramp-Ups: Why Digital Workforce Readiness Matters as Much as Physical Automation
items.description: Third-party logistics (3PL) providers live in a world of constant change. New customer contracts, seasonal peaks, facility expansions, and labor fluctuations can require operations to scale from dozens to hundreds of associates in a matter of weeks. While much attention is often paid to warehouse automation and material handling systems, workforce ramp-up remains one of […] The post Managing 3PL Ramp-Ups: Why Digital Workforce Readiness Matters as Much as Physical Automation appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
Third-party logistics (3PL) providers live in a world of constant change. New customer contracts, seasonal peaks, facility expansions, and labor fluctuations can require operations to scale from dozens to hundreds of associates in a matter of weeks. While much attention is often paid to warehouse automation and material handling systems, workforce ramp-up remains one of the biggest determinants of whether a new operation succeeds or struggles.
The challenge is not simply finding labor. It is enabling new employees to become productive, compliant, and engaged as quickly as possible. As labor markets become increasingly diverse and warehouse networks more complex, technologies such as smart access control systems and learning management systems (LMS) are emerging as important tools for accelerating operational readiness.
For many 3PLs, the launch phase of a new customer operation follows a familiar pattern. Hundreds of workers must complete onboarding, safety training, facility orientation, and role-specific instruction before they can contribute at expected productivity levels. The consequences of delays can be significant. When associates spend excessive time waiting for facility access credentials, searching for training materials, or completing manual onboarding processes, productivity targets become difficult to achieve. Supervisors are pulled away from operational responsibilities to handle administrative tasks, while customer service levels may suffer during the critical startup period.
In today’s competitive logistics environment, customers expect rapid implementation timelines and near-immediate performance. As a result, workforce readiness has become a strategic differentiator rather than simply an HR function.
One area that is often overlooked during warehouse start-ups is facility access. Traditional onboarding processes frequently require physical badge creation, manual verification processes, paperwork reviews, and multiple handoffs before an employee can enter operational areas. These steps may appear minor individually, but they create friction when multiplied across hundreds of workers. Smart access platforms can streamline the process by digitizing credential management and automating approval workflows. Workers can complete portions of the onboarding process before arriving onsite, while managers gain visibility into who has completed required certifications and who is authorized to enter specific work areas.

items.title: OlmoEarth v1.3: State-of-the-art embeddings for the whole planet
items.excerpt:
🤗 Models | 📄 Tech Report | 📊 Data | 💻 Code | 🌎 Embeddings Explorer | 🗺️ Interactive story
Today, we’re releasing OlmoEarth v1.3 , a state-of-the-art satellite embedding model. Alongside OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re sharing precomputed, annual embeddings for the whole planet (10m, 64- and 128-dimensions), plus a new browser-based tool to explore and customize maps based on those embeddings — the OlmoEarth Embeddings Explorer . This means anyone can put OlmoEarth v1.3 to work right away, from tracking change over time to finding similar places—no sign-in, and no advanced technical knowledge required.
Until now, the primary way to use OlmoEarth was fine-tuning in OlmoEarth Studio: training a model for each task and running it over satellite imagery to make a map. That requires GPU access and the ability to download and store the imagery . Embedding models compress satellite data into ready-to-use features that can be reused cheaply for many tasks.
With OlmoEarth v1.3, we’re excited to give users more ways to explore and engage with planetary artifacts in whatever way suits them best.
An embedding represents what the model learned from millions of images. OlmoEarth v1.3 reads a year of radar (Sentinel-1) and multispectral (Sentinel-2 and Landsat) satellite time series and produces one 128-dimensional vector for every 10-meter pixel on Earth; the first 64 dimensions also work on their own as a smaller embedding.
Foundation models and global embeddings are expensive to produce, and to make sure everyone is able to access the benefits, we’ve computed these embeddings for the entire planet and shared them with the community on Source Cooperative . From there, a crop map, a land-cover map, or a change analysis becomes a lightweight modeling problem: train a small classifier on top and run it locally.
How OlmoEarth v1.3 makes an embedding: a vision transformer reads the satellite data, an Attention Pooler pools it into one vector per patch of land, and a linear layer reduces it to 128 numbers.
We evaluated OlmoEarth v1.3's embeddings against AlphaEarth Foundations (AEF) and Tessera v2 across 27 evaluations, covering six continents and many different tasks. OlmoEarth’s 128-dimensional embeddings score highest on 20 of 27 evals and rank highest overall. The 64-dimensional version, at half the size, still leads on 18 of 27 evals. International buyers are no longer chasing eye-catching showroom prototypes. They are sourcing production-grade robotic systems built for continuous real-world deployment. This transition gains further momentum amid the fair’s overarching themes of innovation-driven […]
items.excerpt:
Seventy years after the inaugural Canton Fair opened for global sample-based procurement, the 140th edition lays bare a pivotal shift within robotics and automation. International buyers are no longer chasing eye-catching showroom prototypes.
They are sourcing production-grade robotic systems built for continuous real-world deployment. This transition gains further momentum amid the fair’s overarching themes of innovation-driven growth, green transition and smart manufacturing.
To put the evolution in perspective: the very first Canton Fair operated out of a 9,600 m² venue and welcomed 1,200 buyers. Today’s event covers 1.55 million m², hosting more than 32 000 exhibitors and roughly 310,000 preregistered overseas buyers.
Phase 1 features 17 purpose-built zones for emerging industries. Its service-robot exhibit hall serves as a concentrated showcase for China’s endtoend robotics supply ecosystem.
Attendees can trace the full industrial supply chain onsite. Tactile feedback sensors, high-performance harmonic reducers, modular joint assemblies and machinevision hardware feed into finished-goods portfolios spanning humanoid robots, dexterous manipulators, powered exoskeletons, firefighting quadruped robots, autonomous inspection platforms and commercialgrade cleaning robots.
Over 11,000 specialised champion enterprises took part, and 64% of exhibitors leverage AI or industrial internet-based technology stacks.
Green-smart integration runs through product development cycles across the floor. Robotic hardware interfaces with new energy mobility and low carbon industrial equipment.
Multiple exhibitors noted rising overseas demand for automation hardware designed to cut operational carbon footprints. Manufacturers of commercial cleaning robots highlighted strong yearoveryear overseas sales growth fuelled by demand for round-the-clock unmanned operation.
Buyer behaviour delivers the clearest industry signal. Industrial, logistics and facilitymanagement delegations spend less time watching scripted showcase demos. Instead, they dig into practical questions around uptime, maintenance cycles, spareparts availability and compliance with regional regulatory requirements.
One hundred and seventy major international buying groups confirmed attendance prior to opening, while newproduct launches for emerging sectors climbed roughly 20%.

items.title: a16z Frontier
items.description: Some of the most important technology waves are still ahead
items.excerpt:
Today we’re announcing that we’re expanding the scope of our new fund beyond crypto startups to the broader category of frontier startups: companies building new technologies and creating markets that may take years to develop. To reflect this, we’re renaming a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier. This is an expansion: we will continue to invest in crypto and related ventures and advocate for sensible crypto regulation.
When we started investing in crypto, it was a world of its own. But as blockchains have become more widely used, the lines have blurred and the infrastructure has gradually receded into the background. Wall Street and fintech companies now regularly launch products built on blockchains. Does that make them crypto companies? The label matters less now. It makes more sense to define companies by what they do rather than by the technologies they use.
Our expansion also reflects an approach that has guided many of our investments for years: backing technologies that look futuristic, well before they reach the mainstream. When I joined a16z in 2013, I made these kinds of long-horizon investments a focus. One theme was new computing devices . The growth of smartphones made cameras, sensors, and chips better and cheaper, enabling new devices like drones, AR/VR headsets, and wearables. That theme led to investments in Oculus and drone startups like Skydio and Zipline .
The other was crypto, which I saw as a new wave built on social media and the open source movement. Social media allowed networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum to gain traction from the outside in , as people formed communities without first needing mainstream acceptance. Open source provided the model for software that anyone could inspect, modify, and build on. Blockchains extended that model from software to services and networks. This theme guided our investment in Coinbase and the creation of our crypto funds , as well as later investments in projects like Solana and Uniswap.
Now we are in the middle of another major tech wave centered on AI. The buildout of AI models and infrastructure will continue, but the tech is already sufficiently advanced to spawn a new generation of products and services. No one knows exactly what that generation will look like, but we’re beginning to catch glimpses. We’re especially interested in the new products and markets these advances will enable, including ones that don’t fit into existing categories.

items.description: Newcomer 长文复盘 Anthropic 从 OpenAI 出走团队到即将 IPO 的股权演变。据投资人文件和多位知情人士，多年来风投因公司治理结构和安全优先路线而观望，目前没有任何风投机构持股超过 2%，Anthropic 曾向投资人明确将单一投资人持股控制在该水平以避免话语权集中。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/shd9gpw42uwoxqtenpzhy1je4
items.excerpt:
The Story of Anthropic’s Cap Table: VCs Showed Up Late to the Party, Toting All the Cash They Could Wrangle
Newcomer 长文复盘 Anthropic 从 OpenAI 出走团队到即将 IPO 的股权演变。据投资人文件和多位知情人士，多年来风投因公司治理结构和安全优先路线而观望，目前没有任何风投机构持股超过 2%，Anthropic 曾向投资人明确将单一投资人持股控制在该水平以避免话语权集中。
文章基于投资人文件和多方信源还原 Anthropic 的股权结构，解释了为何风投早期缺席、如今持股均不超 2%。
如果一切按计划进行， Dario Amodei 和他的Anthropic联合创始人将于下个月敲响纳斯达克的开市钟，以纪念公司IPO。他们的庆祝无疑将迎来风险投资家们惯常的击掌与拍背祝贺。
但Anthropic从一小群OpenAI叛将成长为行业领先的巨头、并有望迎来史上最大规模IPO的历程，远比我们在硅谷通常看到的故事要混乱得多。
多年来，风投公司一直拒绝投资Anthropic，担心其不同寻常的公司结构以及对安全而非商业化的执着使其成为一笔糟糕的赌注。根据投资者文件以及六位了解该公司多轮融资的消息人士的说法，如今没有任何一家风投公司持有该公司超过2%的股份。其中一位人士表示，将风投持股控制在该比例以下、以确保没有任何单一投资者拥有过大控制权，是Anthropic向投资者传达的目标。
文章基于投资人文件和多方信源还原 Anthropic 的股权结构，解释了为何风投早期缺席、如今持股均不超 2%。

items.title: METR 与 Redwood Research 红队测试 OpenAI 内部智能体监控系统，发现多个漏洞
items.description: METR 与 Redwood Research 各派一名员工，于 7 月 21 日至 8 月 11 日对 OpenAI 内部失准监测系统开展三周高权限试点压力测试，产出 61 页内部报告。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fcw2s1pdclkgm5kmg2qwginp7
items.excerpt:
Red-Teaming OpenAI's Internal Agent Monitoring Systems
METR 与 Redwood Research 各派一名员工，于 7 月 21 日至 8 月 11 日对 OpenAI 内部失准监测系统开展三周高权限试点压力测试，产出 61 页内部报告。
作者以亲历视角披露对 OpenAI 内部监控系统的压力测试，给出覆盖率估算、漏洞清单和可复用的监控设计原则。
在为期三周的时间里（7月21日至8月11日），一名 METR 员工和一名 Redwood Research 员工开展了一次试点性高权限演练，对 OpenAI 的 内部失准监控系统 进行压力测试。 1 此次演练的产出是一份 61 页的内部报告，已与 OpenAI 的研究人员和安保人员共享， 2 报告主要聚焦于估算受监控的智能体推理所占比例，以及智能体原则上能否禁用或破坏监控系统。演练针对的是截至7月21日（含当日）已存在的内部失准监控系统，未评估演练期间正在进行的 变更 。
此次演练涉及深度访问权限。METR 和 Redwood 的员工可以访问 OpenAI 的内部代码库、失准监控提示词/配置详情以及内部文档，并与监控、安全系统和安保团队的大约十几名研究人员和工程师进行了技术访谈。为获得这一级别的访问权限，他们使用 OpenAI 配发的设备开展工作，这些设备从未离开过办公场所，且他们在现场期间全程有人陪同。
METR、Redwood Research 和 OpenAI 将此次演练设计为一次试点，目的是让外部研究人员深度访问内部基础设施，而非就 OpenAI 的监控系统向公众提供有力的透明度说明 3 。因此，我们事先与 OpenAI 商定，只发布一篇相对简短、高层次的公开文章。对于未来版本的此类演练，我们预计将遵循“ 我们与 AI 公司合作的方式 ”中所述的透明度与独立性最佳实践，以提供更有力的公众透明度。
METR 和 Redwood 的员工在截至7月21日（含当日）已存在的异步内部失准监控系统中发现了若干新型漏洞。我们注意到，OpenAI 在我们的演练期间正在扩展其监控系统。我们的发现描述的是我们在7月21日（含当日）及之前所评估的历史系统，而非扩展后系统的当前覆盖范围——此次演练并未确定该覆盖范围。以下是演练中发现的一些示例性摘要：
我们估计，在演练时，来自能力至少与 GPT-5.5 相当的模型的智能体内部 Responses API（为 Codex 等提供支持） 4 流量中，大约 75%–94% 有资格受到监控， 5 不过我们在两个方向上都有很大的不确定性。我们还估计，在用于内部 Codex 智能体的那部分 Responses API 流量中，99.2% 有资格受到监控。
尽管我们获悉，在3月至6月期间，有一部分 RL 训练 rollout 受到了失准监控，但在演练开始时，RL 训练运行并未被监控系统覆盖。
我们估计，未对压缩事件进行监控，很可能导致2026年5月至7月期间约 10% 的有资格内部 Codex 流量未被监控，不过我们对确切比例有很大不确定性，因为在演练时，确定压缩触发了多大比例的监控调用所需的信息在历史上并未被记录。OpenAI 员工在演练开始前已独立发现了这一问题，并在演练期间修复了它。
在演练进行时，监控系统会在智能体将控制权交还给用户时触发，因此在压缩事件未被监控的时间段内，智能体只需继续采取行动，就可以无限期推迟被监控。 6
我们看到了有关监控系统错误率和降载率的信息——提供给我们的信息表明，在演练进行时，监控系统在不到 0.2% 的请求上出错，并且在演练期间的某个 24 小时时段内降载次数为零。
我们发现了一种 Codex 智能体原则上可以绕过 Codex 沙箱和 Auto-Review 的方法，使它们能够采取宿主用户所能采取的任何操作。
我们还发现了一种智能体可以利用的漏洞，该漏洞会阻止数百个近期操作（包括该漏洞本身所涉及的操作）被监控 [漏洞细节已由 OpenAI 隐去]。
我们发现，智能体很可能可以构造输入，利用智能体所看到的轨迹与监控系统所看到的轨迹之间的序列化差异，使监控系统失败（从而不会将该轨迹升级为人工审查）。
我们发现两个可由客户端控制的独立标头，它们会为新智能体禁用监控系统，这可能使智能体能够启动一个不受监控（但在其他方面完全相同）的实例。然而，设置这些标头并创建新智能体实例的行为可能会被监控系统捕获。
我们发现两个不受监控的内部智能体工具，它们被认为具有只读权限——我们发现了一个简单的漏洞利用方法，本可用于颠覆这些限制，并在其沙箱环境中采取任意操作。我们未验证该行为，也未测试它在实践中是否可被利用。
我们验证了监控系统的提示词会查找谋划、监控系统颠覆、破坏、数据外泄、欺骗以及入站/出站提示注入等风险类别。
演练完成后，OpenAI 表示，我们发现的、影响其生产防护体系的所有漏洞均已修复。OpenAI 还 描述 了其监控系统预期覆盖范围随后的重大变化。我们尚未评估这些说法。
基于我们的发现，我们概述了一些监控与控制系统的设计理想，总结如下。总体而言，我们认为未来的监控基础设施应当能够承受高能力内部智能体在规模上蓄意、有策略且持续的攻击。
让逃避监控变得困难。 运行不受监控的请求应需要明确批准使用特定的一组组织/API 密钥，且这些密钥不得用于智能体推理。应按每 N 条消息/分钟对智能体进行监控，而不是等待它们结束回合。
确保本应被监控的流量确实被监控。 仔细记录所有发生的推理，以及其中哪一部分正在被监控——定期将这些日志与监控系统直接生成的日志进行交叉核对，以确保所有本应被监控的内容确实被监控。维护一份所有已知绕过监控方式的清单。确保监控系统看到与智能体相同的上下文。
快速、可靠地响应事件。 为事件响应分配明确的责任归属，并维护清晰的指导方针以减少主观性。尽可能对更多的推理和监控流量保留防篡改且易于搜索的日志。
主动对监控系统进行红队测试。 定期开展控制评估

items.title: PHP2Shell 漏洞披露前黑客已有四天窗口，多国机构紧急响应
items.description: PHP2Shell 漏洞在被披露前四天已遭黑客利用，Calif 与 Wiz 的研究人员发现这些漏洞。OpenAI 称其前沿 AI 在攻击者之前发现了漏洞，并与 PHP、Calif、Wiz 合作验证并开发补丁。NSA 建议无法立即更新的机构将系统离线，英国 NCSC 表示漏洞可能让黑客无需登录凭据即可控制网站服务器，白宫称联邦机构正在评估对政府系统和关键基础设施的潜在影响。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/m34xrhmqj1is6d1v1jna3ed46
items.excerpt:
Hackers got a four-day head start on epic PHP2Shell vulnerability
PHP2Shell 漏洞在被披露前四天已遭黑客利用，Calif 与 Wiz 的研究人员发现这些漏洞。OpenAI 称其前沿 AI 在攻击者之前发现了漏洞，并与 PHP、Calif、Wiz 合作验证并开发补丁。NSA 建议无法立即更新的机构将系统离线，英国 NCSC 表示漏洞可能让黑客无需登录凭据即可控制网站服务器，白宫称联邦机构正在评估对政府系统和关键基础设施的潜在影响。
原文汇总了 NSA、NCSC 和白宫对 PHP 漏洞的处置表态，还引出 OpenAI 关于前沿 AI 发现漏洞的争议。
“这些漏洞通常提供了通往服务器文件系统或数据库的直接路径，”NSA表示。“如果无法立即更新，建议各组织在能够完全缓解之前将系统下线。”
美国两家网络安全组织Calif和Wiz的研究人员发现了这些漏洞。Alphabet旗下的Wiz估计，这种受影响的编程语言驱动了全球约70%的网站。
“鉴于这些缺陷的严重性以及PHP的广泛使用，我们认为这是近期记忆中最具影响的安全问题之一，”OpenAI周三表示。“据我们所知，前沿AI在攻击者之前发现了这些漏洞。”
“这凸显了AI如何能够发现具有互联网规模影响的安全缺陷，但同样的能力也可以帮助攻击者快速开发攻击工具和漏洞利用程序，”该AI实验室补充道。
PHP在互联网上的广泛存在，很大程度上是因为使用最广泛的网站建设平台WordPress主要用PHP编写，并依赖它来运行。
英国国家网络安全中心表示，这些漏洞可能允许黑客在无需密码或其他登录凭据的情况下控制网站的服务器。“NCSC鼓励英国组织立即采取行动，”它表示。

items.title: Beyond tree cover: mapping the world’s forest types
items.description: A global map categorizing every 10-meter patch of land on Earth into distinct forest types.
items.excerpt:
A new 10-meter resolution map shows which of the world's forests are natural, planted, or farmed, and how they are changing over time
Protecting the planet's forests starts with a simple question: what type of forest are we looking at? From space, an old-growth rainforest, a eucalyptus plantation, and an oil palm estate can look like the same patch of green. But they hold very different amounts of carbon and biodiversity. Telling them apart, and knowing how each patch has changed over time, shows us where conservation is working and where natural forests are being converted into plantations and farms.
Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research, together with the World Resources Institute (WRI) and the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA), are releasing Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020 , a global map that categorizes every 10-by-10-meter patch of land on Earth into six distinct forest and land-use types, a key baseline for the EU's deforestation regulation. Alongside it, we're sharing an early time series that tracks how these forests changed each year from 2017 to 2025, including where natural forests were replaced by plantations or farms. For the first time, users can see at 10-meter detail worldwide, year by year, not just where forest was lost, but what replaced it: a timber plantation, a tree-crop farm or other land.
All forests store carbon and, together, forests are home to most of the world's land-based plant and animal species. But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history: a primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation that is harvested every decade or two.
Most global maps only indicate whether trees are present. That's a challenge for those trying to protect natural forests. The European Union's regulation on deforestation-free products (EUDR), for example, requires that products like coffee, cocoa or palm oil do not originate from land that was forest in 2020 and has since been converted to agriculture. Similarly, wood products, such as furniture, must also be free of forest degradation: they can't come from primary forests that have since been converted into plantation or planted forests, or from naturally regenerating forests that have since been converted into plantation forests. items.title: 404 Media 分析 PHP2Shell 事件如何改变 AI 时代的攻防格局
items.description: 404 Media 的 Jason Koebler 梳理近一个月安全专家对 AI 挖洞能力引发的"Black October"恐慌。Wiz、Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究者用 AI 发现了 PHP 的 PHP2Shell 漏洞，Cloudflare CEO 称公开公告前 10 小时已见数千次利用尝试，公告后 2 小时内增至数十万，目前达数百万级。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/pe2uqi2ny6l2lukrqzifbtyum
items.excerpt:
AI Is Changing Everything About Hacking. No One Knows What Happens Next
404 Media 的 Jason Koebler 梳理近一个月安全专家对 AI 挖洞能力引发的"Black October"恐慌。Wiz、Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究者用 AI 发现了 PHP 的 PHP2Shell 漏洞，Cloudflare CEO 称公开公告前 10 小时已见数千次利用尝试，公告后 2 小时内增至数十万，目前达数百万级。
作者基于对安全专家的长期报道，梳理了 PHP2Shell 事件前后 AI 改变攻防节奏的多种迹象，并指出漏洞修补的部署速度未必跟上。
在过去一个月的大部分时间里，我交谈和关注的许多网络安全专家发帖时都显得非常恐惧。许多人一直在警告一场由AI驱动的“黑天鹅”事件，对突然发现的大量漏洞感到警觉，也对AI代理和大型语言模型在发现和利用此前未知漏洞方面显而易见的强大能力感到不安。
这些言论从担忧但克制（事情即将变得诡异），到诸如更新软件、确保开启双重认证之类的常规建议，到关于AI驱动攻击的 含糊其辞的发帖 ，到“ 互联网曾经美好过 ”之类的话，再到彻头彻尾的 末日准备者级别的恐惧 。
为了让你了解我所看到的情况，约翰斯·霍普金斯大学教授、世界上最受尊敬的密码学家之一Matthew Green 发帖 说，“我们正处在电影里那种你得把能扔的东西都扔到僵尸面前、希望这能拖慢它们的阶段”，以及“这么多人发现 整个互联网都是干柴 ，而唯一阻止它烧起来的原因是青少年还没找到火柴”，Green指的是，驱动AI工具和代理的黑客与研究人员越来越擅长发现和利用重要系统中的各种漏洞。我还看到许多 AI员工，如前所述，彻底变成了末日准备者 ，建议人们从银行账户中取出钱、断开互联网连接、购买耐储存食品、囤水、把钱换成黄金和现金，并购买手摇应急收音机。
而所有这些帖子都出现在人们使用AI驱动的工具发现PHP漏洞 之前 ——PHP是支撑互联网大部分内容的编程语言。在过去几天里， eMudhra （一家提供网站安全证书的印度实体）、 Node.js （PHP的替代方案）、 Gitlab （一个软件开发平台）、 Plex （媒体服务器软件）、 Railway （一家云服务提供商）、 OpenCode （一个编码代理平台）以及其他多家公司和服务中都被发现了重大漏洞或问题，不过，理所当然地，这些都没有PHP中的漏洞那样受到关注——该漏洞被称为PHP2Shell，由 Wiz 、 Calif 和 OpenAI 的研究人员使用AI发现。
Cloudflare是一家 对互联网整体健康状况有广泛洞察 的服务商，其CEO Matthew Prince 发帖 说，“在[PHP2Shell]被公开宣布前的10个小时里，我们在整个Cloudflare网络上看到了数千次利用它的尝试。在宣布后的45分钟内，这一数字跃升至数万次，2小时内达到数十万次，现在已达到数百万次。”
发生的事情如此之多、如此之快，以至于对我——一个报道和编辑安全与黑客相关新闻已有十年的人来说——都难以完全理解正在发生什么、对接下来可能发生什么有清晰判断，或预测这将走向何方。而我认为，在我写下这些的时候，这大体上就是我们目前的处境。
但已经很清楚的是，广义上的人工智能已经从根本上改变了攻击性黑客行为和防御性网络安全。这并不是因为人工智能有了意识，也不是因为人类失去了对它的控制，也不是因为出现了“流氓智能体”的“蜂群”，而是因为人工智能正在证明一件我们一直都知道的事：运行互联网、我们的设备、我们的账户以及我们生活的许多软件都是脆弱的、过时的，或者存在人类从未注意到的安全漏洞，或者是由某家公司某个人安装的，而那个人六年前就离开了公司，岗位已经换了四次，现在没人知道怎么找到他，也不知道怎么更新它。这并不意味着在人工智能帮助下发现的所有漏洞都是显而易见或微不足道的；熟练的黑客和研究人员借助人工智能工具， 似乎在发现漏洞方面比单靠人类更强 。但关键在于，人工智能和大语言模型让对互联网进行本质上的暴力破解变得极其容易；如果把每一款软件都比作一扇门，人工智能让转动每一扇门把手、看看它是否没锁变得异常简单，即便是人类从未真正费心尝试打开的建筑也不例外。我们正以惊人的速度认识到，不仅有些锁很容易撬开，在某些情况下门是大敞的，或者墙上有个大洞。最近一连串有人用人工智能入侵 自己的物联网设备 来运行新软件的事件表明，在某些情况下，实际上不需要任何专业知识就能用人工智能入侵某些东西。
与此同时，我们看到了 “消融”人工智能模型 的兴起，这类模型被设计成不会说“不”，以及开放权重模型，它们可用于渗透测试和潜在的攻击性黑客行为，而不受许多现成商业模型中存在的防护限制。
在解释 PHP 漏洞 发现的博客文章中，OpenAI 表示这些发现凸显了“人工智能如何能发现具有互联网规模影响的安全漏洞，但同样的能力也能帮助攻击者快速开发攻击工具和漏洞利用程序”。OpenAI 基本上主张，它是以合乎伦理的方式完成所有这些研究的，并且其 发现开启了一个“防御者窗口” ，让政府和关键基础设施能够为该漏洞的披露做好准备。“研究人员发现漏洞，以合乎伦理的方式向公司披露，公司修复它”是网络安全领域的首选做法，但人工智能正在缩短这一切的窗口期，正引导更多人以更低的门槛做更多的研究，并让漏洞发现和漏洞修复都变得快得多。至于这些修复是否真的会被各个公司更快地部署，则是另一个复杂得多的问题。在许多情况下，答案很可能是：不会。
AI 也让这一切变得更加难以预测。安全公司 Chainguard 因违反 PHP 漏洞披露的禁令而受到批评 ，因为它在漏洞被正式披露前数小时就发布了修复方案。批评者 包括 PHP 基金会 表示，这可能让攻击者在网站所有者有机会保护其系统之前就弄清楚如何利用这些问题。Chainguard 首席执行官 Dan Lorenc 在 LinkedIn 的一篇帖子

items.title: The AI Bubble Meets the Supply Chain: Where Is the Productivity?
items.description: When Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, warned this week that financial bubbles almost certainly exist within artificial intelligence, Wall Street took notice. But the more interesting part of his argument was directed at corporate America. Companies are opening their bills from OpenAI and Anthropic and asking whether the technology is producing enough productivity to justify […] The post The AI Bubble Meets the Supply Chain: Where Is the Productivity? appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
When Ken Griffin, founder of Citadel, warned this week that financial bubbles almost certainly exist within artificial intelligence, Wall Street took notice. But the more interesting part of his argument was directed at corporate America. Companies are opening their bills from OpenAI and Anthropic and asking whether the technology is producing enough productivity to justify the cost. For transportation, warehousing, and supply chain executives, that is a familiar question.
Speaking at Citadel’s Future of Global Markets Conference in New York on October 20, Griffin described an uneven ability among companies to extract value from AI. Yet he also acknowledged that financial bubbles frequently accompany technological revolutions. Both observations can be correct. AI may be attracting more investment than its economics can currently support while becoming increasingly valuable to the businesses using it.
There is a further possibility worth considering: an AI infrastructure correction could ultimately benefit supply chain operators if excess computing capacity and greater competition make intelligent software less expensive.
The scale of spending is remarkable. Reuters , citing Anthropic’s draft IPO prospectus, reported an $80.7 billion net loss for the first half of 2026, including a $72 billion noncash accounting charge tied to convertible financing instruments. The company also disclosed commitments of at least $518 billion over a decade for cloud services, computing, and infrastructure. The headline loss should not be confused with an equivalent cash operating loss, but the infrastructure obligations are substantial.
This matters beyond Silicon Valley because the cost and availability of AI models influence the economics of enterprise software. Across transportation management systems (TMS), warehouse management systems (WMS), and supply chain planning (SCP), suppliers are introducing conversational interfaces, predictive tools, intelligent exception management, and autonomous agents. Some capabilities are valuable today. Others remain demonstrations of what may eventually be possible.
For technology buyers, the challenge is separating a useful feature from a financial return. A sophisticated model does not, by itself, move a shipment, replenish inventory, or clear a warehouse backlog. The value appears when better information changes an operating decision and that decision improves performance.

items.title: What Maersk and Adidas Reveal About Event Logistics
items.description: Maersk’s account of 38 adidas installations highlights the importance of integrated scheduling, handoff ownership and exception management. The post What Maersk and Adidas Reveal About Event Logistics appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The most unforgiving delivery window in logistics may not be the next-day parcel commitment. It may be the window before a major event begins. When the crowds arrive, the installation must already be complete. An explanation about a late truck will not improve the customer experience.
That is what makes Maersk’s recently published account of its work with adidas interesting. According to an October 19 case study, Maersk Ground Freight coordinated 38 time-critical installations across North America during the summer of 2026 as adidas created fan experiences around its Giant Trionda activation.
In Maersk’s description, the assignment was larger than moving freight between cities. It connected transportation, warehousing, scheduled deliveries, installation, and on-site management. adidas chose a single Maersk team to coordinate the work rather than managing separate vendors for each activity.
This is a supplier-reported success story, not an independent operational benchmark. Still, the execution model illustrates a broader lesson: the final outcome often depends more on the management of handoffs than on any single transportation leg.
Most supply chains have at least some flexibility. Inventory can sometimes be repositioned, orders reprioritized, or service recovered after a delay. Major sporting events and temporary brand installations offer much less room to recover.
Equipment and materials may need to arrive during specific site access windows. Venue rules, security, staging space, labor availability, and installation sequencing can constrain how work occurs. For example, a truck arriving early might be unable to unload, while a late arrival could disrupt a crew, another contractor, or the opening schedule. These are illustrative risks, not reported incidents from the adidas project.
The logistics challenge therefore includes both physical movement and synchronization. Transportation plans must reflect when a site can actually receive goods and when installation personnel will be available to use them.
Across 38 installations, this becomes a network problem. Multiple locations, schedules, and contingencies have to be tracked consistently, even as local conditions differ.
Traditional logistics contracts often divide responsibility among providers. One company manages storage, another handles line-haul transportation, a local carrier makes delivery, and a separate contractor handles installation.

items.title: You are the Team — Anekha Sokhal, Moshi
items.description: How Moshi turns market data into actionable insights, and why AI tools have to fit the trader’s workflow.
items.excerpt:
Tickets and applications now live for AIE CODE - the last flagship AIE of the year.
When Anekha Sokhal traded energy derivatives, staying on top of the market meant tracking more information than any person could read. Now, as CEO of Moshi, she is building the tool she wished she had: a recommendation engine that connects market information to what matters for a trader’s book.
At AI Engineer New York, Anekha joins swyx to discuss her path from mathematics and JPMorgan to founding Moshi, and why useful AI needs to fit the way people actually work. She describes Moshi as what might happen if Bloomberg, Claude and Netflix had a baby: market data, an interface for working with it, and recommendations tailored to the trader.
They also talk about trusted sources, document extraction, building versus buying models, and the pressure on AI engineers who are told, “you are the team.” Anekha shares what she learned from customer conversations at the conference and why meeting users comes before hiring.

items.title: Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，检验语音智能体能否准确采集姓名、电话等实体信息
items.description: Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，测量语音智能体能否正确采集、识别错误并修复姓名、电话号码、地址和邮箱等细节，包含 10 种实体类型共 200 个任务，并与 𝜏-i18n 一样覆盖六种语言。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/fjyan16f0mvfywabd78m70hv3
items.excerpt:
𝜏-Entity: Can voice agents get the details right?
Sierra 发布 𝜏-Entity 基准，测量语音智能体能否正确采集、识别错误并修复姓名、电话号码、地址和邮箱等细节，包含 10 种实体类型共 200 个任务，并与 𝜏-i18n 一样覆盖六种语言。
Sierra 自建基准和论文量化了语音智能体在准确采集姓名、电话等细节上的失败率，并给出可迁移的验证策略效果数据。
语音智能体能够处理日益复杂的对话，但有时导致通话失败的其实很简单：把一个名字、电话号码或电子邮件地址弄对。我们在 𝜏 -Voice 中反复看到这一瓶颈：智能体弄错一个细节，还没能提供帮助就先在身份验证上失败了。
今天我们推出 𝜏-Entity ，这是一个基准，用于衡量智能体能否正确捕获细节、识别出细节可能有误，并修复错误。
𝜏-Entity 在十种实体类型（包括姓名、电话号码、地址和电子邮件）的 200 项任务上测试语音智能体。每通电话聚焦于单个字段，来电者配合，在被要求时会准确拼写。大多数通话耗时不到两分钟。
每项任务都从一个缺失的值开始。智能体必须向来电者询问该值并正确提交。成功要求存储的值与预期值完全一致。我们改变三件事：值本身的难度、来电者的行为（如纠正和重新开始）以及音频环境。
然后我们测量 Pass³：智能体能否在常规、高噪声和高语音条件下成功完成同一任务。
在汇集全部六种 𝜏 -i18n 语言的 𝜏-Entity 排行榜上，GPT Live 1 领先：它在 60.3% 的常规通话中正确捕获该值，但仅在 34.0% 的任务中在全部三种条件下都成功。Gemini 3.8 Live 和 Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 在常规条件下分别达到 43.8% 和 44.2%，在全部三种条件下则降至 19.5% 和 24.0%。
仅英语更容易：GPT Live 1 在常规通话中达到 74.0%，在全部三种条件下达到 47.5%。西班牙语、葡萄牙语和印地语接近英语，对 Gemini 和 Grok 而言得分高于英语，但韩语 Pass³ 降至 3.5–8.5%，普通话在各智能体中降至 12.5–24.5%。
当人们不确定自己是否听对时，他们会放慢速度、请对方重复、拼写名字或确认所听到的内容。智能体只识别出部分应当放慢速度的理由，而漏掉了其他理由。
在 𝜏-Elicitation 论文中，我们将验证努力度量为智能体在通话中进行复述和拼写请求的次数，然后比较了该行为在熟悉与不熟悉实体、简单与困难值、嘈杂与干净环境以及不同来电者声音下的表现。
该研究中的智能体对某些类型的难度做出了适应：在各系统中，它们对困难和陌生实体验证得更仔细。但只有 Grok 在噪声下验证得更多，且没有任何系统对它最难应对的来电者声音投入更多验证努力。
在论文中，我们还测试了规定一种验证策略能否弥合差距。规定的顺序是：询问，让来电者拼写该值或复述，确认并纠正，然后提交。
当智能体自行选择验证策略时，在所有三种条件下，只有 14–41% 的任务成功。规定的顺序将这一比例提升至 37–54%，根据配置不同，提升了 14–31 个百分点 。但额外的谨慎需要付出时间代价：每次调用会多花 21–28 秒。
即使智能体意识到自己可能出错，也不保证能恢复。在论文的行为分析中，智能体验证的初始错误捕获中，最终只有 24–37% 被纠正。有时智能体会重复同样的错误。另一些时候，它会用一个新的错误值替换原来的值。只有当智能体能正确利用答案时，追问才有用。
当一次调用需要多个字段时，错误也会累积。在论文的多字段研究中，尽管单个字段的准确率仍为 75%，但三字段调用的成功率只有 53%。在针对相同多字段任务的另一项对比中，验证每个字段并允许重试将成功率从 64% 提高到 82%。由于该干预措施结合了验证和重试，我们无法区分各自贡献了多少。
方向是明确的：可靠的语音智能体需要识别不确定性、验证正确的内容，并在错误发生时真正修复错误。
这些结果指向两个机会：更好地决定何时以及如何验证，以及在出错时进行更可靠的纠正。只有当智能体能利用答案来纠正其捕获的内容时，追问才有帮助。
这并不意味着每次交互都需要尽可能长的验证过程。规定的验证提高了可靠性，但花费更多时间。挑战在于知道何时需要额外努力，并让这种努力发挥作用。
𝜏-Entity 提供了受控任务，用于衡量跨实体类型、呼叫者行为和环境方面的进展。我们与 𝜏-i18n 一同推出它，并且它已经覆盖相同的六种语言。
Sierra 自建基准和论文量化了语音智能体在准确采集姓名、电话等细节上的失败率，并给出可迁移的验证策略效果数据。

items.description: Wiz 披露 2026 年 10 月有攻击者使用开源自主渗透测试框架 ARTEX 针对多家 IT 和软件厂商，活动与微软报告的中国国家级关联组织 Storm-0940 重叠，并已扩展到其他软件领域的供应链攻击尝试。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/n6afjfxhq6vadobu4p0lm6tzm
items.excerpt:
ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
Wiz 披露 2026 年 10 月有攻击者使用开源自主渗透测试框架 ARTEX 针对多家 IT 和软件厂商，活动与微软报告的中国国家级关联组织 Storm-0940 重叠，并已扩展到其他软件领域的供应链攻击尝试。
Wiz 基于自家日志复盘了开源 AI 渗透测试框架 ARTEX 被实战滥用的完整手法，给出了可复用的检测规则和 IOC。
2026年10月期间，我们发现一名攻击者使用与ARTEX（一个自主AI渗透测试代理）相关的工具，针对多家IT和软件供应商发起攻击。该活动聚焦于身份提供商（Okta、Entra、Cognito）以及对Microsoft 365集成的滥用。我们观察到其在多个环境中反复尝试发现身份验证绕过、枚举API并访问（目标供应商的）客户数据。
我们的观察与微软 近期关于Storm-0940的报告 存在重叠，该组织是一个与中国政府关联的攻击者，与近期 涉及被盗供应商凭证及下游Microsoft 365租户的供应链攻击 有关。\
然而，我们还额外观察到相同的基础设施、工具和攻击模式针对整个行业。通过对已识别的TTP和IOC进行关联分析，我们还发现同一攻击者正将其尝试的供应链入侵扩展到其他软件领域。
在本博客中，我们将描述使用ARTEX的攻击者在多个环境和云提供商中应用的可重复模式和方法，并附上来自真实攻击的示例。
ARTEX是一个开源的自主渗透测试框架。一名中国开发者于2026年7月在GitHub上发布了它，并于当年9月赢得了百度的“Agent+”红队挑战赛。在实际操作中，操作员提供目标和目的。随后规划代理选择下一步行动，工作代理运行 nmap 、 curl 和 Impacket 等工具，每个结果都会汇入一个共享的资产与发现图谱。
攻击者在数周内就采用了它。ARTEX的痕迹出现在9月下旬 对韩国银行的攻击 以及10月 对日本企业的攻击 中。 微软 和 Zscaler 此后将其与两个不同的攻击者关联起来。开发者于 10月8日将该工具转为闭源 。彼时，该代码已有超过12,000个分支。
测绘应用： 下载JavaScript包、暴露的source map、运行时配置以及Swagger/OpenAPI文档，以发现内部API路由和应用功能。
探测身份验证： 反复发起登录流程，操纵OAuth回调和state参数，测试未签名的JWT，并探测SSO和Microsoft 365专用端点。
攻击身份提供商和登录流程： 对企业Okta和Entra ID环境进行密码喷洒，并针对内部和专有应用的登录页面。
测试租户隔离： 尽可能使用一次性电子邮件地址注册账户，然后操纵可预测的标识符，以探测访问控制缺陷和未经授权的跨租户数据访问。
我们使用通过 Wiz无代理工作负载检测 收集的HTTP访问日志，以及AWS Cognito事件、Entra登录活动和Okta身份验证日志等身份提供商日志，分析了这些攻击模式。

不久之后，它开始按名称调用内部 API 路由。这些路由名称唯一出现的地方，就是它刚刚下载的 source map。

第二个令牌解码后不过是 {"alg":"none"} 和 {"email":"test@test.com"} 。该代理在两分钟内用这个载荷对 60 多种 SSO 路由变体发起了密集请求。
在 AWS Cognito 上，我们观察到了与专有应用中账户恢复滥用相呼应的模式。这一活动体现在 InitiateAuth 、 ForgotPassword 和 ResendConfirmationCode 等事件中。这些请求来自与早前攻击中观察到的相同的用户代理组合，包括 boto 和 python-urllib 这类看似无害的编程客户端。
该代理还尝试直接创建新身份，调用 AWS Cognito SignUp API，同时轮换其用户代理池。
我们还追踪到一场针对众多已观察目标的大规模密码喷洒活动。该活动不区分 IDP，同时攻击 Entra 和 Okta，并表现出若干独特的 AI 驱动特征。
该活动具有持久性和高度自动化。部分会话持续 24–30 小时，当 IP 被封锁时，新地址会在几分钟内出现。
在一次会话中，该代理轮换了同一 SSO 端点的十几种变体 （ /sso 、 /sso/ 、 /sso/login 、 /sso/jwt 、 /jwt/sso… ），每种变体都分别携带和不携带同一伪造令牌，速率约为每秒一个请求。当某个登录页面开始对该活动进行速率限制时，该代理干脆切换到同一主机上的另一个端点继续操作。
这种多样性，结合一致的攻击模式和与 ARTEX 相关的指标，帮助我们将跨多个组织的活动关联起来。
尽管这些尝试大多失败了，但真正的威胁在于其方法论。人类攻击者受限于时间和疲劳，而自主智能体不会放弃。它只会不断迭代，直到找到一个薄弱点。
